attribution.note: A section headline Zitron wrote in his own newsletter post. It is his claim, not a quote of someone else.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the firm 'will only lose it money' and correctly leaves out the normative 'shouldn't accept customers'. 'No good solutions' is partly a present-tense assessment, but treating the whole as a conditional forecast on added capacity is a reasonable reading.

contract.note: The plain reading (attributable costs exceed attributable returns, counting only delivered capacity) is an ordinary, fair reading of firm language. The speaker gave no metric or deadline, so how 'lose money' is defined decides the result.

evidence.note: S-1 filing (company disclosure) showing compute was delivered in H1 2026. This shows the antecedent was met but does not isolate returns attributable to the added capacity.
Anthropic's own May 2026 announcement of higher usage limits. It challenges 'no solutions' but is a company statement and says nothing about sustained reliability or expansion economics.

Secondary summary of the S-1: company-wide H1 operating cash flow was positive, the June quarter had operating income, and there was a large net loss from fair-value charges. None of this is measured per unit of added capacity.

reviews.rationale: Firm forecast with no deadline. Capacity was delivered (e1), so the antecedent is met. But no evidence separates the costs and receipts attributable to that expansion. Company-wide cash flow and operating profit (e3) and the raised limits (e2) are context, not the matched accounting the early-resolution rule needs. No conclusive event has occurred, so the claim stays open.
